title: Grateful Dead Live at Kresge Plaza, M.I.T. on 1970-05-06
lineage: MSR (MIT Reels) 1/2 Track Mono > Otari MX 55 2 track (playback) > TC 2000 Studio Effects Processor (A>D only, no effects) > Sonic Solutions (20bits) > Sony SBM-2 > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the historic May 6 1970 MIT free concert, highlighted by a monster Dancin' and soaring Good Lovin'.
ai_review.review: The show is widely praised as one of the best performances of 1970 – the band is tight, the jams on Dancin', Good Lovin' and the St. Stephen/NFA sequence are described as ferocious and unforgettable, and the emotional weight of Morning Dew resonates with the Kent State context. The recording, taken from a sound‑board feed (sbd), is generally called crisp, clear and “monster” sounding despite occasional vintage tape roughness.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5‑star and describe it as a top‑tier 1970 performance; recording quality is repeatedly called excellent or very good, giving a combined weighted score well above 4.5.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix from the MIT radio feed; some reviewers note a vintage “choppy” or “rough” edge but overall the sound is vivid and loud with very good instrument separation.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is described as flowing naturally, with high energy transitions (e.g., St. Stephen into NFA) and a powerful second half that builds to emotional peaks; the historic free‑concert atmosphere adds extra momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for ripping guitar work – “monster sound”, metallic twang, ferocious riffs, and leading the jams with intensity.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lauded for his lead‑bass approach, driving improvisation and tight interplay with Jerry that fuels the band’s fire.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned mainly for dual vocal work on "Next Time You See Me"; no strong criticism or praise beyond that.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen's organ/harmonica is highlighted as vital (especially on Good Lovin') and his quirky mic comment adds character; Bobby’s supportive keys are noted on the mellow middle of Dancin'.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as a “soundscape” and crucial to the overall groove, especially during the extended jams.
